chunks: Indeed, God is more merciful to His creation than to compel His creation to commit sins and then punish them for them; and God is mightier than to will a matter and have it not come into being.

He (the narrator) said: So they (peace be upon them both) were asked: 'Is there a third position between compulsion and pre-determination?' They both said: 'Yes — more extensive than what is between the sky and the earth.'

key_terms.أرحم: More merciful — a theological argument from divine attributes: God's mercy precludes compulsion to sin followed by punishment
key_terms.أعز: Mightier/more exalted — a theological argument that God's omnipotence precludes the possibility of His will being unfulfilled
key_terms.الجبر: Jabr — theological doctrine of absolute compulsion; the view that humans have no free will and are entirely compelled by God
key_terms.القدر: Qadar — here used for the Mu'tazilite view of absolute free will and human self-determination (distinct from its more common use as divine decree)
key_terms.منزلة ثالثة: A third position — the Shia doctrine affirming human moral responsibility within a framework that avoids both extremes

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia position on free will and divine compulsion (jabr and qadar) in Islam?
ai.summary: Imams al-Baqir and al-Sadiq (peace be upon them) affirm the Shia theological doctrine of 'al-amr bayn al-amrayn' — the position between absolute compulsion (jabr) and absolute free will/pre-determination (qadar). They first establish God's transcendence: His mercy precludes Him from compelling creation to sin and then punishing them, and His power precludes His will from being unfulfilled. When asked whether a third position exists between jabr and qadar, the Imams confirm it emphatically, describing it as more vast than the space between heaven and earth. This teaching, central to Shia theology, affirms human moral responsibility while upholding divine sovereignty.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman, from someone else, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> both having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is more Merciful with His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures than Compelling His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures upon the sins, then He<sup>azwj</sup> Punishes them upon these; and Allah is Mightier than for Him<sup>azwj</sup> to Intend a matter, so it does not come into being’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So they<sup>asws</sup> were both asked, ‘Is there a third status between the Compulsion and the Pre-determination?’ They<sup>asws</sup> both said: ‘Yes, more extensive than what is between the sky and the earth’.
